newsitem.title: UK: Glaxo slips further as downgrades weigh.
newsitem.headline: Glaxo slips further as downgrades weigh.

text.p: Shares in Glaxo Wellcome Plc were down 7-1/2p to 935p by 1200 GMT continuing to feel the weight of recent broker downgrades, dealers said.
"There hasn't been a lot of good news about on the stock and some investors, especially the Americans, have been selling it in drips and drabs," one senior dealer said.
"We've also had a few downgrades over the past few weeks and that hasn't helped, although no one has really taken the knife out on profit projections."
Glaxo shares have fallen 12 percent since reaching a 12-month high of 10.65 stg in October.
Last Thursday the shares were under pressure after talk that broker HSBC James Capel had reduced its profits forecasts to reflect the recent strengthening of the pound.
That news came on the heels of a Merrill Lynch downgrade on the stock on November 28.
Merrills cuts its rating on Glaxo to "neutral" from "accumulate" on the basis of a reassessment of the potential sales of its new products to hit the market in 1998-99, dealers said.
